# Copilot Studio What's New — captured 2026-07-03
# (source ms.date 2026-06-25; page updated 2026-06-30)

## June 2026 [NEW since prior scan — cache previously topped at May 2026] — REPORTABLE (primary tier)
- **New agent experience (production-ready preview)** — enhanced orchestration runtime for improved response quality/reasoning, available alongside the classic experience. New agent build model/runtime entity. (AISPM)
- **Microsoft IQ** in the new agent experience — connects an agent to organizational data: emails, calendar events, files, Teams messages, and people information. New knowledge/data-grounding connection surface. (AISPM/AIDR HIGH)
- **Skills** in the new agent experience — modular, self-contained sets of instructions; create once, add to multiple agents, export as Markdown file or package to share. New reusable-capability entity + sharing/supply-chain surface. (AISPM)
- **Memory** in the new agent experience — persistent per-user context; captures user preferences/patterns, stores them per user, applies over time. New per-user memory store (holds user data/PII). (AISPM)

## May 2026 [already cached / prior scans]
- Computer use GA (browser + desktop automation on behalf of users); prompt node; Microsoft 365 Copilot node in workflows; consent-based voice recording; agent inventory schema (admin discovery/audit); agent readiness/issue status page; async agent-flow responses; (preview) Microsoft Entra agent identities per agent; computer-use standalone tools; Mistral Medium 3.5 model option.

## April 2026 [already cached]
- Real-time voice agents (preview); agent-to-agent (A2A) protocol GA; agent evaluation REST API; GPT-5.5 Reasoning (Deep); Analytics Viewer role; hold/resume voice.

## Earlier (cached): Work IQ (Mar 2026), Bing Custom Search knowledge, MCP server support (Oct 2025), Client SDK, code interpreter, Entra agent identities (preview Nov 2025), Fabric data agents, tool groups.

Updated: 2026-07-03 — NET-NEW reportable: the June 2026 "new agent experience" rollout (new orchestration runtime) and its three new entity types — Microsoft IQ (org-data grounding), Skills (reusable/exportable capabilities), and Memory (per-user persistent store).
